newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-YOUNG AUSTRALIAN GIVEN GRAND SLAM BAPTISM OF FIRE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-YOUNG AUSTRALIAN GIVEN GRAND SLAM BAPTISM OF FIRE.

text.p: Australian teenager Lleyton Hewitt, at 15 years and 10 months the youngest men's player at the Australian Open, was handed a tough lesson in grand slam tennis by experienced Spaniard Sergi Bruguera on Tuesday.
Hewitt, who qualified for the Open, was beaten 6-3 6-4 6-3 in the first round by the former two-time French Open champion.
"It was not a tough match," said unseeded Bruguera.
"He has no power because he is 15 years of age. But he is very talented and has good hands," he said.
"I tried not to get overawed and do my best," said Hewitt. "Once the match starts, he is just another player."
The Adelaide schoolboy had been hoping to emulate world number two Michael Chang, who won his first grand slam match at the U.S. Open in 1987 at 15 years and six months.
Chang, the second seed in Melbourne, went on to win the French Open in 1989 as a 17-year-old.
Although common in the women's game, the strength in depth in men's tennis makes it rare for a player in his mid-teens to break through into the main draw at grand slam events.
Fifteen-year-old Russian Anna Kournikova, the youngest woman in the draw, made an early exit on Monday, losing 6-2 6-2 to 12th seed Amanda Coetzer of South Africa.
